observation.visible_scene: A sunlit wooden walkway/deck made of horizontal planks with narrow gaps between them. The planks are covered by the shadows of overhead foliage. To the right of the close framing there is bare soil with a curved root/log and a few green sprouts. The clip is split into two framings joined by an apparent editing transition: the first is a tight close-up of four planks with sharp, well-defined leaf shadows; the second is a wider, more top-down view of about seven or eight planks with softer, dappled shadows and grass visible along both edges.
visible_changes: During the close-up portion (frames 1-19) the plank layout and camera framing stay essentially fixed while the sharp leaf shadows shift and flicker slightly from frame to frame (small positional changes of the shadow shapes, not of the boards).

Around frames 20-23 the image changes framing: the close-up shadows and the right-side root/soil fade out while a wider plank layout and grass on both sides fade in, with both views briefly superimposed (translucent greenery at the left edge and a ghosted shadow pattern). This overlap is consistent with a cross-dissolve between two shots rather than a continuous optical zoom, because the two views have different backgrounds (root/soil vs. grass) and different shadow textures.
During the wide portion (frames 24-41) the camera framing is again stable, with only the dappled shadows drifting and changing intensity slightly frame to frame.
No person, animal, or moving object crosses the boards; the only visible motion is the changing shadow pattern.
outside_clip_unknowns: What is casting the shadows (the foliage itself is never shown) and what moves it.
Whether the close and wide framings are the same physical deck or two different locations.
The moments before frame 1 and after frame 41, including whether the dissolve is the only edit in the source.
uncertain_details: The exact nature of the mid-clip change (cross-dissolve vs. a cut with a brief overlay) cannot be fully confirmed from sampled frames alone.
The slight shadow drift could be foliage movement or minor exposure/lighting change; the cause is not visible.
Whether the camera is perfectly still or has very small handheld jitter is not determinable from these frames.
